# MLX-DLSS source attribution

The SR backbone code in `src/features/sr/source_backbone` adapts the network math and weight layout from [MLX-DLSS](https://github.com/iamwavecut/MLX-DLSS/tree/7870371e8bf6c03967213f1a5d40db6c5a3bee38), commit `7870371e8bf6c03967213f1a5d40db6c5a3bee38`, under Apache-2.0. It replaces Swift and MLX operations with CUDA kernels and decodes the original FP16 words into the layouts those kernels read.

The reviewed source files include `Sources/DLSSMLX/DLSSSuperResolution.swift` (SHA-256 `b448d95bd90a8e45287bdf7da3bcb51c175d02aeb9e9a7bb5209523cf33d923a`) and `python/mlxdlss/tools/package_dlss_sr.py` (SHA-256 `b44e100c47f8c20f3e47cdf45a28cb70326fc3debe2a928292dd7bd87852ebfd`). The vendored `ptx_metal.py` comes from `python/mlxdlss/tools/ptx_metal.py` (upstream SHA-256 `0e69c989174080abff66854a5b56d2fe07bbad646041b8276ec944b98ade86f8`). RenderWeave added optional emission hooks for CUDA scalar rounding, approximate instructions and typed parameter reads. The default Metal emission still matches the registered reference hash. The license and notice are kept alongside this file. Original NVIDIA weights are read from the registered assets at runtime.
